chapters.title: Chapter 1: Foundations of Louisiana Insurance Contract Law
chapters.description: Introduces core principles governing insurance policies under Louisiana law, with emphasis on contract formation, policy terms, cancellation, and lapse for nonpayment.
subtopics: Insurance policy as a contract under the Louisiana Civil Code
Interpretation of insurance contracts and ambiguities
Conditions precedent, premium payment obligations, and grace periods
Cancellation versus nonrenewal and lapse
Burden of proof on cancellation and continuation of coverage

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Premium Finance Agreements and the Louisiana Statutory Framework
chapters.description: Explains Louisiana’s statutory scheme for insurance-premium financing, including the roles and rights of insureds, premium finance companies, and insurers.
subtopics: Structure and purpose of insurance-premium finance agreements
La. Rev. Stat. § 9:3550: scope, key definitions, and policy aims
Default, cure periods, and prerequisites to cancellation
Allocation of authority among insurer, insured, and finance company
Recordkeeping and proof requirements for finance companies

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Agency and Powers of Attorney in Premium-Financed Cancellations
chapters.description: Covers Louisiana agency law principles relevant to a finance company’s authority to cancel a policy under a power of attorney.
subtopics: Mandate (power of attorney) under the Louisiana Civil Code
Creation, scope, and proof of agency authority
Acts taken under a mandate and effect on third parties
Limitations and revocation of authority
Interaction between contractual POA clauses and statutory requirements

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Statutory Mechanics of Cancellation Under La. R.S. 9:3550
chapters.description: Details the step-by-step statutory process for cancelling premium-financed policies, including required notices and certifications.
subtopics: Ten-day notice of cancellation to the insured upon default
Contents of the finance company’s certification to the insurer
Required notices to loss-payees, lienholders, and governmental agencies
Permissible delivery methods: mail, private carrier, electronic mail
Timing: fixing the cancellation date and preserving the cure period

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Strict Compliance Doctrine in Louisiana Insurance Cancellations (Delatte, Eaglin, Britten, Hodges)
chapters.description: Surveys key Louisiana appellate decisions establishing strict adherence to statutory cancellation procedures and the consequences of defects.
subtopics: Delatte v. Lemotte: insistence on strict statutory compliance
Eaglin v. Champion Insurance: defects render cancellation ineffective
Britten v. Reavis: functions of strict compliance—exact timing and cure window
Hodges v. Colonial Lloyd’s: cancellation upon receipt mechanics
Strict vs. substantial compliance in Louisiana insurance law

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Notice, Delivery, and ‘Receipt’ in Insurance Cancellations
chapters.description: Analyzes how Louisiana law treats delivery and receipt of cancellation notices and certifications, including evidentiary showings and practical methods.
subtopics: Meaning of ‘receipt’ and evidentiary proof of delivery
Use of mail, private carriers, and acknowledgment practices
Affidavits, certificate of mailing, and business records
Third-party and internal delivery arrangements
Consequences of defective or untimely receipt

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Electronic Communications and Compliance
chapters.description: Explores the legal effect of electronic transmissions in satisfying statutory notice and receipt requirements.
subtopics: Louisiana’s Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (La. R.S. 9:2601 et seq.) and E-SIGN basics
When electronic records and signatures satisfy legal requirements
System-to-system communications, automated processes, and server logs as evidence
Defining electronic ‘receipt’ and time of delivery
Risk allocation and best practices for electronic compliance

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Louisiana Insurer Duties of Good Faith and Fair Dealing
chapters.description: Provides background on statutory and jurisprudential duties governing insurer conduct toward insureds and third parties.
subtopics: La. R.S. 22:1892 and 22:1973: prompt payment, misrepresentation, and bad faith standards
Good faith performance of contractual obligations
Relationship between statutory compliance and bad-faith exposure
Remedies: penalties, attorney’s fees, and damages
Third-party claimants and limits of insurer duties

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Interpreting Louisiana Statutes in a Civilian System
chapters.description: Outlines interpretive methods Louisiana courts use to construe statutes, including textual canons and reliance on civilian principles.
subtopics: Civil Code arts. 9–13: text, intent, and application of clear language
Plain-meaning rule and use of legal dictionaries
Expressio unius, negative-implication reasoning, and avoiding judicial additions
Harmonizing related provisions and legislative purpose
Weight of administrative and industry practice

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Erie, Choice of Law, and Predicting State Law in Federal Court
chapters.description: Explains how federal courts sitting in diversity apply and predict state law, including the role of intermediate appellate decisions.
subtopics: Erie doctrine and its application to substantive state law
Hierarchy of Louisiana authorities: statutes, Civil Code, Supreme Court, appellate courts
Using intermediate appellate decisions as persuasive evidence of state law
When federal courts make an ‘Erie guess’
Deference and limits when state law is unsettled

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Certification of State-Law Questions to State Supreme Courts (with Jefferson v. Lead Industries Ass’n)
chapters.description: Covers the procedure, standards, and strategic considerations for certifying unsettled state-law questions from federal court to a state supreme court.
subtopics: Authority and procedures for certification in the Fifth Circuit
Jefferson v. Lead Industries Ass’n: cautionary approach to certification
Criteria: determinative nature, novelty, and importance to state policy
Timing, phrasing, and effect of certified answers
Standard of review for certification decisions

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Federal Subject-Matter Jurisdiction and Removal in Class Litigation
chapters.description: Introduces the bases for federal jurisdiction over class actions removed from state court and the mechanics of removal.
subtopics: Diversity jurisdiction basics and the Class Action Fairness Act (CAFA)
Removal procedure and timeliness
Remand standards and burden allocations
Effect of jurisdictional posture on applicable law
Supplemental jurisdiction and party alignment issues

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Summary Judgment Standards and Appellate Review
chapters.description: Summarizes the Rule 56 framework and how appellate courts review summary judgments and related rulings.
subtopics: Rule 56: burdens of production and persuasion
Viewing evidence in the light most favorable to the nonmovant
Cross-motions and partial summary judgment
De novo review on appeal
Interplay with state-law issues resolved at summary judgment

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Using Precedent and Authority in Insurance Disputes
chapters.description: Explains how courts synthesize statutory text, case law, and secondary sources in insurance disputes involving procedural compliance.
subtopics: Precedent hierarchy and persuasive authority
Analogical reasoning from related fields (e.g., delivery and carriage concepts)
Role of industry custom versus statutory command
Burden-shifting through documentary compliance
Common litigation pitfalls in cancellation disputes
